# The Lights That Never Rush

## Scripture

*"But do not forget this one thing, dear friends: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day."* — 2 Peter 3:8

## Reflection

Step outside on a clear September night and look up. That faint smudge of light in the constellation Andromeda is the Andromeda Galaxy—2.5 million light-years away. The photons landing on your eyes tonight began their journey before humanity existed. And yet, from God's vantage point, that ancient light is simply arriving on time.

We live in a world that worships speed. Faster downloads, quicker answers, instant results. When God seems slow to answer a prayer or fulfill a promise, we grow restless, wondering if He has forgotten us. But Peter reminds us that God's timing isn't measured by our clocks. What feels like delay to us may be perfect patience to Him.

Consider the autumn sky. The stars don't rush across the heavens; they move with quiet, steady faithfulness, night after night. The Andromeda light didn't hurry—it simply traveled faithfully until its appointed arrival. God's promises work the same way. They are never late. They are never early. They arrive exactly when His wisdom determines.

If you are waiting on the Lord this season, take heart. The same God who set galaxies in motion and governs their patient journeys is governing yours. His promises are traveling toward you even now, and they will not fail to arrive.

## Prayer

Father, thank You for the patient faithfulness of Your creation and Your promises. When waiting feels long, remind me that Your timing is perfect and Your love never hurries past Your wisdom. Give me grace to trust the light that is still on its way. In Jesus' name, amen.
